newsitem.title: USA: Hewlett-Packard to announce new small business program.
newsitem.headline: Hewlett-Packard to announce new small business program.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co. Monday will unveil a customer service program to help small businesses set up computer networks.

Under its Small-Business Technology Initiative, Hewlett-Packard will match small companies with consultants and computer resellers at no charge. The consultants will help the companies set up PCs, connect printers and install computer networks, HP executives said.
"We're trying to build on the brand and reputation we have in this market," said Kathleen Tandy, HP's small business PC marketing manager.
The marketing program should help HP get a bigger share of the so-called small-office, home-office PC market, Tandy said.

HP will set up a site on the World Wide Web where small business customers type in their zip code and get the phone numbers of local consultants. The Web site also will have areas with tips on how to run small businesses, Tandy said.
HP also will unveil Monday two new laser printers and two devices that will make laser-printer operation cheaper for small businesses.

Tandy said the company will introduce two more products in its flagship printer line-up, the LaserJet 6P and the LaserJet 6L. Along with those, the company will unveil the LaserJet companion, a $249 device that turns a stand-alone laser printer into a copier and optical character recognition scanner.

HP also will introduce the Printserver, a $149 device that manages the printing tasks of several PCs hooked up to one laser printer. Until now, a dedicated PC was required to manage printer operation in a network.
